children.name: Aceros
children.description: A genus of large, long-tailed hornbills found in the forests of South and Southeast Asia. Males have distinctive rufous or orange plumage on the head and neck, while females are black. They are important seed dispersers for many rainforest tree species.

children.name: Aceros nipalensis
children.description: The rufous-necked hornbill (Aceros nipalensis) is a species of hornbill in Bhutan, northeastern India, especially in Arunachal Pradesh, Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It is locally extinct in Nepal due to hunting and significant loss of habitat. There are less than 10,000 adults left in the wild. With a length of about, it is among the largest Bucerotine hornbills. The underparts, neck and head are pigmented as a rich rufous in the male, but black in the female.

children.name: Aceros corrugatus

children.name: Aceros cassidix
children.description: Aceros cassidix (Sulawesi hornbill) is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Anorrhinus
children.description: Anorrhinus — a genus of hornbills in the family Bucerotidae.

children.name: Anorrhinus galeritus
children.description: The bushy-crested hornbill is a bird in the hornbill family. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Anorrhinus tickelli
children.description: Tickell's brown hornbill, also known as the rusty-cheeked hornbill, is a species of hornbill found in forests in Burma and adjacent western Thailand. Austen's brown hornbill is sometimes considered as a subspecies of Tickell's brown hornbill.

children.name: Anorrhinus austeni
children.description: Anorrhinus austeni (Austen's Brown Hornbill) is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Anthracoceros
children.description: Asian hornbills with glossy black plumage and large, heavy bills typically in contrasting shades of ivory, yellow and black. They are forest-dwellers that feed mainly on fruit but also take small animals. Their loud, raucous calls are a prominent sound in tropical Asian forests.

children.name: Anthracoceros albirostris
children.description:
The oriental pied hornbill (Anthracoceros albirostris) is an Indo-Malayan pied hornbill, a large canopy-dwelling bird belonging to the family Bucerotidae. Two other common names for this species are Sunda pied hornbill (convexus) and Malaysian pied hornbill.
The oriental pied hornbill is considered to be among the smallest and most common of the Asian hornbills. It has the largest distribution in the genus and occurs in the Indian subcontinent and throughout Southeast Asia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. Its diet includes fruit, insects, shellfish, small reptiles and small mammals and birds including their eggs.

children.name: Anthracoceros convexus
children.description:
The oriental pied hornbill (Anthracoceros albirostris) is an Indo-Malayan pied hornbill, a large canopy-dwelling bird belonging to the family Bucerotidae. Two other common names for this species are Sunda pied hornbill (convexus) and Malaysian pied hornbill.
The oriental pied hornbill is considered to be among the smallest and most common of the Asian hornbills. It has the largest distribution in the genus and occurs in the Indian subcontinent and throughout Southeast Asia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. Its diet includes fruit, insects, shellfish, small reptiles and small mammals and birds including their eggs.

children.name: Anthracoceros coronatus
children.description: The Malabar pied hornbill (Anthracoceros coronatus), also known as the lesser pied hornbill, is a bird in the hornbill family, a family of tropical near-passerine birds found in the Old World.

children.name: Anthracoceros malabaricus
children.description: A hornbill found in the Western Ghats of India.

children.name: Anthracoceros malayanus
children.description:
The black hornbill (Anthracoceros malayanus) is a species of bird of the hornbill family Bucerotidae. It lives in Asia in Brunei Darussalam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand.
The species has a selectiveness towards the environment and resources when it comes to reproduction. It is a lowland specialist. This organism will only start breeding and nesting when there is a large supply of fruits available, and in trees of larger size. When there are limited resources available, and may curtail nesting for years when there is a low availability of fruits(4). It is the major seed disperser for Durio graveolens, a species of durian. The connection is strong enough to reflect in some of the common names for the fruit: The Kenyah and Dayak peoples call it durian anggang (lit. 'hornbill durian'), and in Malay it is called durian burong/durian burung (lit. 'durian bird'). It also has a role in seed disbursement for Vitex pinnata.

children.name: Anthracoceros marchei
children.description: The Palawan hornbill (Anthracoceros marchei) is a large forest bird endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Anthracoceros montani
children.description: The Sulu hornbill (Anthracoceros montani), or Montano's hornbill, is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae.

children.name: Anthracoceros lemprieri
children.description: Anthracoceros lemprieri is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Berenicornis
children.description: A monotypic genus of striking white-crested hornbill found in Southeast Asian lowland forests. The single species is one of the most exquisitely plumaged hornbills, with a brilliant white head and tail contrasting with a black body.

children.name: Berenicornis comatus
children.description: The white-crowned hornbill (Berenicornis comatus), also known as the long-crested hornbill or white-crested hornbill (leading to easy confusion with the African white-crested hornbill), is a species of hornbill.

children.name: Buceros
children.description: Large, spectacular hornbills with enormous casques atop the bill, which in some species are solid and used for aerial combat. The genus includes the most iconic Asian hornbills, revered in many cultures as symbols of majesty and good fortune. Their wingbeats produce a distinctive whooshing sound audible from a distance.

children.name: Buceros bicornis
children.description: The great hornbill (Buceros bicornis), also known as the concave-casqued hornbill, great Indian hornbill or great pied hornbill, is one of the larger members of the hornbill family.

children.name: Buceros rhinoceros
children.description: The rhinoceros hornbill (Buceros rhinoceros) is a large species of forest hornbill (Bucerotidae).

children.name: Buceros hydrocorax
children.description: The rufous hornbill (Buceros hydrocorax), also known as the Philippine hornbill and locally as kalaw (pronounced KAH-lau), is a large species of hornbill endemic to the Philippines (the largest hornbill in the country).

children.name: Buceros abyssinicus
children.description: A northern ground hornbill of the Sahel region.

children.name: Buceros leadbeateri
children.description: A large ground hornbill found in southern and East Africa.

children.name: Buceros vigil
children.description: Buceros vigil (Helmeted Hornbill) is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Bycanistes
children.description: Medium to large African hornbills with distinctive black-and-white plumage and large, often colourful casques. They are highly vocal and social, often moving through the forest canopy in small flocks. Their loud, piping calls are a characteristic sound of African forests.

children.name: Bycanistes bucinator
children.description: The trumpeter hornbill (Bycanistes bucinator) is a medium-sized hornbill, with length between , characterized by a large grey casque on the bill, smaller in females.

children.name: Bycanistes fistulator
children.description: The piping hornbill (Bycanistes fistulator) is a bird in the hornbill family.

children.name: Bycanistes cylindricus
children.description: The brown-cheeked hornbill (Bycanistes cylindricus) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in Ivory Coast, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Togo. Its natural habitats are tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests, plantations, and secondary growth forests. It is threatened by habitat destruction, as timber is harvested and the forests become increasingly fragmented.

children.name: Bycanistes albotibialis
children.description: The white-thighed hornbill (Bycanistes albotibialis) is a species of hornbill. It is found in Angola, Benin, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Nigeria, Sudan, and Uganda. It is sometimes considered to be a subspecies of the brown-cheeked hornbill.

children.name: Bycanistes brevis
children.description: The silvery-cheeked hornbill (Bycanistes brevis) is a large species of hornbill found in Africa. Silvery-cheeked hornbills are residents of the tall evergreen forests of East Africa from Ethiopia to South Africa. In Zimbabwe it is threatened by habitat destruction and its presence in South Africa is marginal, but it remains locally fairly common, especially in the northern and central parts of its range.

children.name: Bycanistes subcylindricus
children.description:
The black-and-white-casqued hornbill (Bycanistes subcylindricus), also known as the grey-cheeked hornbill, is a large black and white hornbill. It has an oversized blackish bill with a large casque on top. The female is slightly smaller than the male and has a significantly smaller casque. It is a monogamous species, and pairs nest in suitable tree cavities. The female usually lays up to two eggs. The diet consists mainly of figs, fruits, insects and small animals found in the trees.
Widespread and still locally common, the black-and-white-casqued hornbill is assessed as least concern on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.

children.name: Bycanistes sharpii
children.description: Bycanistes sharpii (Sharp) is a hornbills species found in Africa region.

children.name: Bycanistes temminckii
children.description: Bycanistes temminckii (Temminck) is a hornbills species found in Africa region.

children.name: Bycanistes subquadratus
children.description: Bycanistes subquadratus is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Ceratogymna
children.description: Large, predominantly black hornbills of West and Central African forests with striking blue facial skin and large casques. They are primarily frugivorous and play a crucial role in forest regeneration through seed dispersal.

children.name: Ceratogymna atrata
children.description: The black-casqued hornbill (Ceratogymna atrata), or black-casqued wattled hornbill, is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found fairly commonly across sub-Saharan Africa, being known from Sierra Leone and Liberia in Western Africa (as well as most of the West African nations along the Gulf of Guinea), south to Angola and east to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda. They are currently considered of near threatened, and their population is declining.

children.name: Ceratogymna elata
children.description:
The yellow-casqued hornbill (Ceratogymna elata), also known as the yellow-casqued wattled hornbill, is found in the rainforest of coastal regions of West Africa, for example in Côte d'Ivoire. It is threatened by habitat loss.
The yellow-casqued hornbill is one of the largest birds of the West African forest, with adults weighing up. They live mainly in the forest canopy, rarely feeding on the ground. They live in small family groups containing at least one adult male and female, with one or two immature birds, though they sometimes gather in larger flocks to exploit a major food supply such as an ant or termite nest.

children.description: Ceratogymna cylindricus (Brown-cheeked Hornbill) is a hornbills species found in Africa region.

children.description: Ceratogymna bucinator (trumpeter hornbill) is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Lophoceros
children.description: African hornbills characterised by a relatively small casque and a distinctive pale bill often with a dark tip or stripe. They are adaptable birds of savanna, woodland, and forest edge, and are among the most frequently encountered hornbills across Africa.

children.name: Lophoceros nasutus
children.description: The African grey hornbill (Lophoceros nasutus) is a member of the hornbill family of mainly tropical near-passerine birds found in the Old World.

children.name: Lophoceros pallidirostris
children.description: The pale-billed hornbill (Lophoceros pallidirostris) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in Angola, DRC, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zambia.

children.name: Lophoceros alboterminatus
children.description: The crowned hornbill (Lophoceros alboterminatus) is an African hornbill.

children.name: Lophoceros fasciatus
children.description:
The Congo pied hornbill (Lophoceros fasciatus) is a bird of the hornbill family, a family of tropical near-passerine birds found in the Old World.
The Congo pied hornbill is native to the Congo Basin. This is a bird of mainly forest habitats. The female lays up to four white eggs in a tree hole, which is blocked off during incubation with a cement made of mud, droppings and fruit pulp. There is only one narrow aperture, just big enough for the male to transfer food to the mother and the chicks.

children.name: Lophoceros hemprichii
children.description: Hemprich's hornbill (Lophoceros hemprichii) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Uganda.

children.name: Lophoceros jacksoni
children.description: A hornbill found in East Africa.

children.name: Lophoceros camerunensis
children.description: Lophoceros camerunensis (Cameroon Hornbill) is a hornbills species found in Africa region.

children.name: Lophoceros griseus
children.description: A grey hornbill from West Africa.

children.name: Lophoceros hartlaubii
children.description: A hornbill from West and Central Africa.

children.name: Lophoceros semifasciatus
children.description: Lophoceros semifasciatus (West African Pied Hornbill) is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Ocyceros
children.description: Ocyceros — a genus of hornbills in the family Bucerotidae.

children.name: Ocyceros birostris
children.description: The Indian gray hornbill is a common hornbill found on the Indian subcontinent. It is mostly arboreal and is commonly sighted in pairs. It has grey feathers all over the body with a light grey or dull white belly.

children.name: Ocyceros gingalensis
children.description: The  Sri Lanka grey hornbill is a bird in the hornbill family and a widespread and common endemic resident breeder in Sri Lanka. Hornbills are a family of tropical near-passerine birds found in the Old World.

children.name: Ocyceros griseus
children.description: The Malabar gray hornbill is a hornbill endemic to the Western Ghats and associated hills of southern India. They have a large beak but lack the casque that is prominent in some other hornbill species. They are found mainly in dense forest and around rubber, arecanut or coffee plantations.

children.name: Penelopides
children.description: Penelopides — a genus of hornbills in the family Bucerotidae.

children.name: Penelopides affinis
children.description:
The Mindanao hornbill (Penelopides affinis), also known as the Mindanao tarictic hornbill, is a medium-small species of hornbill found in the canopy of rainforests on Mindanao, Dinagat, Siargao and Basilan in the southern Philippines. All five Philippine tarictics were once considered a single species. Its population declining due to habitat destruction, hunting and the illegal wildlife trade.
It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess Mindanao hornbills under Philippine Law RA 9147.

children.name: Penelopides manillae
children.description:
The Luzon hornbill (Penelopides manillae), sometimes called Luzon tarictic hornbill, is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is endemic to forests on Luzon and nearby islands in the northern Philippines. All five Philippine tarictics were once considered a single species. It is declining due to habitat destruction, hunting and the illegal wildlife trade.
It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess these birds under Philippine Law RA 9147.

children.name: Penelopides mindorensis
children.description: The Mindoro hornbill is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is endemic to forests on Mindoro in the Philippines found in tropical moist lowland forests. As is the case with all five Philippine tarictic hornbills, formerly considered to be just one species.

children.name: Penelopides panini
children.description:
The Visayan hornbill (Penelopides panini) is a hornbill found in tropical moist lowland forests of the Philippines in the Western Visayas region which includes the islands of Panay, Negros and formerly as well as the island of Masbate, and formerly Ticao, in the Philippines. As is the case with all five Philippine tarictic hornbills, formerly considered to be just one species, it is declining due to habitat destruction, hunting and the illegal wildlife trade.
It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess these birds under Philippine Law RA 9147.

children.name: Penelopides samarensis
children.description:
The Samar hornbill (Penelopides samarensis) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in forests on the islands of Samar, Calicoan, Leyte and Bohol in the east-central Philippines. As is the case with all Philippine tarictic hornbills, it has been considered a subspecies of Visayan hornbill Alternatively, it is considered a subspecies of Mindanao hornbill.
It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess these birds under Philippine Law RA 9147.

children.name: Penelopides basilanica
children.description: Penelopides basilanica is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhinoplax
children.description: A monotypic genus of endangered hornbill with a solid, front-heavy casque made of keratin, unlike the hollow casques of most other hornbills. The Helmeted Hornbill is unique for the intense red colour of the casque, which is produced by the bird preening its uropygial gland and rubbing the secretion into the casque.

children.name: Rhinoplax vigil
children.description: The helmeted hornbill (Rhinoplax vigil) is a very large bird in the hornbill family.

children.name: Rhyticeros
children.description: Large, predominantly frugivorous hornbills of Southeast Asian forests, characterised by a wrinkled or folded casque on the upper bill. Males have bright yellow or orange facial and throat skin, while females have blue or green skin. They are important seed dispersers for many rainforest trees.

children.name: Rhyticeros undulatus
children.description: The wreathed hornbill (Rhyticeros undulatus) is an Old World tropical bird of the hornbill family Bucerotidae, also called bar-pouched wreathed hornbill due to its distinctive blue-black band on its lower throat sac.

children.name: Rhyticeros cassidix
children.description: The knobbed hornbill (Rhyticeros cassidix), also known as Sulawesi wrinkled hornbill, is a colourful hornbill native to Indonesia.

children.name: Rhyticeros narcondami
children.description: The Narcondam hornbill (Rhyticeros narcondami) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae.

children.name: Rhyticeros plicatus
children.description:
Blyth's hornbill (Rhyticeros plicatus), also known as the Papuan hornbill, is a large hornbill inhabiting the forest canopy in Wallacea and Melanesia. Its local name in Tok Pisin is kokomo.
Previously, this hornbill was placed in the genus Aceros. It has often been lumped with the plain-pouched hornbill (R. Subruficollis), and sometimes considered to include the Narcondam hornbill (R. Narcondami) and the wreathed hornbill (R. Undulatus) as subspecies.

children.name: Rhyticeros subruficollis
children.description:
The plain-pouched hornbill (Rhyticeros subruficollis) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in forests of the Dawna Range and the Tenasserim Hills of southern Myanmar, adjacent parts of western Thailand and northern Peninsular Malaysia.
The Oriental pied Hornbill is a nest competitor of the plain-pouched hornbill. They primarily nest in tetrameles and fig trees.

children.name: Rhyticeros everetti
children.description: Sumba hornbill ( ), or known natively as Julang (in Sumba languages) is a large bird belonging to the family of , endemic and native to the Indonesian island of Sumba.

children.name: Rhyticeros waldeni
children.description: Rhyticeros waldeni is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Tockus
children.description: Small to medium-sized hornbills of African savannas and woodlands, typically with a long, decurved bill and a relatively small casque. They are the most terrestrial of the arboreal hornbills, often foraging on the ground for insects and small vertebrates.

children.name: Tockus albirostris
children.description: Tockus albirostris (White-billed Hornbill) is a hornbills species found in Africa region.

children.name: Tockus bradfieldi
children.description: Tockus bradfieldi (Bradfield) is a hornbills species found in Africa region.

children.name: Tockus damarensis
children.description: The Damara red-billed hornbill (Tockus damarensis) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in southwest Angola and northern Namibia. All five red-billed hornbills were formerly considered conspecific.

children.name: Tockus deckeni
children.description: Von der Decken's hornbill (Tockus deckeni) is a hornbill found in East Africa, especially to the east of the East African Rift, from Ethiopia south to Tanzania. It is found mainly in thorn scrub and similar arid habitats. Jackson's hornbill is often treated as a subspecies of it. It was named after the German explorer Baron Karl Klaus von der Decken.

children.name: Tockus erythrorhynchus
children.description: The northern red-billed hornbill (Tockus erythrorhynchus) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found from southern Mauritania through Somalia and northeast Tanzania. There are five species of red-billed hornbills recognized, but all five were once considered conspecific and some authorities still classify the others as subspecies of Tockus erythrorhynchus.

children.name: Tockus flavirostris
children.description: The Eastern yellow-billed hornbill (Tockus flavirostris), also known as the northern yellow-billed hornbill, is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found in Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda. It resembles the southern yellow-billed hornbill, but has blackish (not pinkish) skin around the eyes.

children.name: Tockus jacksoni
children.description: Jackson's hornbill (Tockus jacksoni) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is only found in North West Kenya and North East Uganda. Except for the dense white spots on the wing-coverts, it resembles, and is often considered a subspecies, Von der Decken's hornbill.

children.name: Tockus kempi
children.description: The western red-billed hornbill (Tockus kempi) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found from Senegal and Gambia to southern Mauritania and western Mali. There are five species of red-billed hornbills generally recognized now, but all five were once considered conspecific. Some authorities still categorize the group as Tockus erythrorhynchus with the remaining four as its subspecies

children.name: Tockus leucomelas
children.description: The southern yellow-billed hornbill (Tockus leucomelas) is a hornbill found in southern Africa.

children.name: Tockus monteiri
children.description: Monteiro's hornbill (Tockus monteiri) is a species of hornbill that is native to the dry woodlands of southwestern Africa. It is a common, near-endemic species in Namibia, with a total population estimated at 340,000 individuals.

children.name: Tockus rufirostris
children.description: The southern red-billed hornbill (Tockus rufirostris) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae, which is native to the savannas and dryer bushlands of southern Africa. It is replaced by a near-relative, the Damara red-billed hornbill, in the arid woodlands of western Namibia. All five red-billed hornbills were formerly considered conspecific.

children.description: Tropicranus albocristatus (White-crested Hornbill) is a bucerotidae species found in its native region.
